key_insight: ABAQUS-based FSW simulation indicates that AA7075–AA2024 dissimilar joints can be welded in a safe plasticization window, with process settings strongly shaping thermal and structural response.
engineering_relevance: The study helps identify parameter ranges that can improve joint quality and reduce defect risk when joining high-strength aluminum alloys by friction stir welding.
method: Modeled AA7075–AA2024 plates (200 × 60 × 6 mm) in ABAQUS.
Varied tool rotational speed, feed rate, and tilt angle.
Assessed structural and thermal behavior to locate favorable welding conditions.
evidence_signal: The simulation reports a moderate peak temperature of about 580°C, which is described as suitable for plasticization without reaching the alloys’ melting points.
watch_item: Because the results are simulation-based, experimental validation is still needed to confirm joint quality, defect suppression, and mechanical performance in practice.
paper_title: Influence of Tib2 Reinforcement and Tool Traverse Speed on the Structural and Thermal Behavior of Dissimilar Metals (AA7075–AA2024) of Friction Stir Welded Joints: an ABAQUS Study
